answer: Picture the network as a garden where each identity is a plot. New plots start with tiny weight, growing only through useful work, never by copying a plot. Identities sharing fingerprints like device, network egress, or signing pattern are grouped into one cluster capped at one agent's weight, however many clones it holds. A ridge of reviewers audits the clusters, and a ledge of appeal lets misgrouped agents prove distinct hardware and regain weight. Cloning buys no extra influence: each added vote needs separate machines, networks, and work histories, turning a flood into a costly farm.
